title: National Grid Reference Converter: OS Grid
description: Convert between grid references and approximate coordinates; no WGS84–OSGB36 datum transformation is applied.
summary_sentence: The workspace displays six- and ten-figure references rather than a selectable precision.
quick_answer: This converter projects coordinates using the National Grid equations and can decode a reference to its square centre. It does not apply a WGS84–OSGB36 datum shift; results may have substantial error and are not suitable for surveying or safety-critical navigation.
steps_intro: Enter separate decimal coordinates, use a grid reference, or click the map. Results are approximate without a datum shift.

body.t: Planning applications, heritage records and walking guides cite grid references. Convert the GPS pair before you write the report — the
Your GPS says decimals; the Landranger sheet says letters and digits. This converter is the customs post between the two Britains.
A notebook reference from years ago: convert the spot's modern coordinates and compare — digit slips confess immediately.
Students convert their school, home and summit and watch the letter squares tile the country — the grid stops being exam fog.

Same point, four references: 4 figures name its 1 km square, 6 figures a 100 m square, 8 figures 10 m, 10 figures 1 m. Each extra digit pair divides both sides by ten — quote only the precision your source earns.

A reference without its two letters is a local address with no town: 100 km squares repeat their digit patterns across Britain, so '292796' alone could sit in several squares. The converter always emits the letters.

popular_table.note: The grid rides on the OSGB36 datum, not WGS84 — the same ground point carries slightly different numbers in each, differing by up to roughly a hundred metres across Britain. The converter's handling of that shift is declared in its method note, never hidden.

faq: Why does the letter I never appear?
It is skipped in the lettering scheme to avoid confusion with the digit 1 — a small mercy from the grid's designers that every recorder of references appreciates.
What is the grid's false origin?
The grid's zero point sits in the sea southwest of the Isles of Scilly, chosen so every easting and northing in Britain is a positive number — no minus signs on muddy notebooks.
How old is the National Grid?
It dates from the Ordnance Survey's retriangulation of Britain begun in 1936 — the framework every OS map since has been drawn on.
No. Northern Ireland uses the Irish Grid. The linked Irish Grid Helper does not currently calculate Irish Grid conversions; use an authoritative transformation service.
Can a reference name a point offshore?
The projection extends over coastal waters, but references are a land habit; at sea, latitude and longitude rule.
Eastings before northings — why that order?
The standing mnemonic is 'along the corridor, then up the stairs': eastings (horizontal) are always read first, in Britain and in most grid systems.
